walkthroughs.body_html:
Consequences Of Uses Of Computing — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Consequences Of Uses Of Computing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Consequences Of Uses Of Computing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which UK Act makes unauthorised access illegal?
options: Data Protection Act
Computer Misuse Act 1990
Copyright Act
Freedom of Information Act
Software patents
Personal data
Network bandwidth
Open source code

mcqs.q: What is the main advantage of asymmetric encryption?
options: It is impossible to break.
Secure key exchange without sharing a secret in advance.
O(log n).
It is faster than symmetric encryption.

mcqs.q: What happens when 11111111 + 1 is computed in an 8-bit register?
options: The computer crashes.
It just becomes 100000000 normally.
Overflow - the result requires 9 bits but only 8 are available.
O(log n).

mcqs.q: What is the worst-case complexity of bubble sort?
options: O(log n).
It is impossible to break.
O(n squared).
O(n) because it just passes through the list.
